correctness.rationale: PASS: For N finite disjoint supported nonnegative wells W_Y, disjointness gives exact ||W_Y||_(3/2)=N^(2/3)||v||_(3/2). Radial v with L²(0,rho) profile is L^(3/2)(R³) by compact support/Hölder. For u∈H¹(R³), Hölder and 3D Sobolev yield integral W_Y|u|²<=C_S N^(2/3)||v||_(3/2)||grad u||². Therefore q_H[u]>=0 for all admissible geometries when 0<lambda<=1/(C_S N^(2/3)||v||_(3/2)); compactly supported L^(3/2) form perturbation has essential spectrum [0,infty), so inf sigma(H)=0 for all those Y. For sufficiently large fixed loop length relative to support radius, regular polygon and a noncongruent small smooth loop deformation retain disjoint wells, giving two tied geometries, contradicting a literal unrestricted unique maximizer. Proof analytic, not relying on experiments. A zero resonance at threshold is possible but does not change inf sigma=0.

originality.rationale: PASS, narrowly qualified: Exner Conjecture 5.3 in materially inspected 2023 original explicitly states a unique regular-loop maximizer for two and three dimensions; its discussion independently notes that in 3D a single regular attractive well needs critical coupling for binding. The novel claim is the uniform all-admissible-geometries N-dependent explicit Sobolev nonbinding plateau and consequent missing binding hypothesis for that exact literal global uniqueness assertion, not the general textbook Sobolev inequality or existence of single-well thresholds. Older point-interaction optimization binds by a different mechanism, not a regular potential counterexample. The concession about a restricted interpretation of principal eigenvalue is essential; no false assertion that binding-regime conjecture is disproved.
residual_risks: A restrictive interpretation of principal eigenvalue could exclude unbound configurations, reducing the result from literal counterexample to necessary binding hypothesis; this interpretation must accompany any presentation.
Uniform cutoff is sufficient only; no claim of optimal coupling threshold or uniqueness/nonuniqueness in binding regime.
Relevant geometry variations require fixed length sufficiently large for pairwise support disjointness.
